response.title: Can I use my old Jackery solar panels with a new EcoFlow or Bluetti power station?
response.answer:
Yes — in many cases, you can use your old Jackery solar panels with a new EcoFlow or BLUETTI power station. You may just need a cable adapter.

The important thing is to check electrical compatibility, not just whether the connectors fit.

What determines compatibility?

Specification

	

What to check




Voltage (Voc)

	

Must not exceed the power station's maximum solar input voltage.




Current (Isc)

	

Check against the station's solar input current limits.




Wattage

	

Determines how much charging power is available; the station may cap how much it accepts.




Connector

	

Jackery often uses DC barrel connectors, while many EcoFlow and BLUETTI models use XT60, XT60i, or MC4.




Polarity

	

Adapter wiring must match the power station's positive and negative terminals.

For example, a Jackery SolarSaga 100W panel might be electrically compatible with an EcoFlow DELTA or RIVER, but require a DC8020-to-XT60 adapter.

Example: Jackery SolarSaga specifications

Jackery has several revisions of its panels, so specifications vary by model.

These are from Jackery's published specifications. 
Jackery Europe
+1

BLUETTI also explicitly supports third-party solar panels on compatible models, provided the input specifications and connectors match. 
BLUETTI - BLUETTI US
+1

One caution: If you have multiple Jackery panels, don't connect them in series or parallel until you've checked the combined voltage and current. A series connection can exceed a power station's voltage limit, potentially damaging it.

The important thing is to check **electrical compatibility**, not just whether the connectors fit.

## What determines compatibility?

| Specification | What to check |
|---|---|
| **Voltage (Voc)** | Must not exceed the power station's maximum solar input voltage. |
| **Current (Isc)** | Check against the station's solar input current limits. |
| **Wattage** | Determines how much charging power is available; the station may cap how much it accepts. |
| **Connector** | Jackery often uses DC barrel connectors, while many EcoFlow and BLUETTI models use XT60, XT60i, or MC4. |

For example, a Jackery SolarSaga 100W panel might be electrically compatible with an EcoFlow DELTA or RIVER, but require a DC8020-to-XT60 adapter.

## Example: Jackery SolarSaga specifications

Jackery has several revisions of its panels, so specifications vary by model.

| Panel | Operating voltage | Open-circuit voltage |
|---|---:|---:|
| SolarSaga 100W (JS-100C) | 20V | 24.8V |
| SolarSaga 200W (JS-200D) | 20.2V | 25V |

BLUETTI also explicitly supports third-party solar panels on compatible models, provided the input specifications and connectors match. <Cite refs={["turn688776search1","turn688776search40"]}/>

**One caution:** If you have multiple Jackery panels, don't connect them in series or parallel until you've checked the combined voltage and current. A series connection can exceed a power station's voltage limit, potentially damaging it.
